Really cool fusion of Vampire Survivors and Risk of Rain 2, probably my favorite game in the "Survivors" genre. A lot of the flavor text and humor is really grating but easy to look past. That's probably my only small complaint.

I've played many Survivor-like games, and Megabonk is one I can't recommend in its current state. It falls off hard after Tier 1.

If you want to succeed a reasonable amount of times, the game becomes restarting for the same items every run. There's very little build diversity, and, past a certain point, the point of the game becomes chasing scores on the leaderboard.

Also worth mentioning is that there's an important movement tech (bunny hopping). It's easy to perform on mouse and keyboard, but strenuous on a gamepad. The other movement tech (strafing) is more strenuous, and can cause motion sickness.

These can likely be addressed through future patches. The dev seems great, and has created a game many people love. My experience may not be universal, but I'm sharing it because these are things I wish I knew prior to purchasing.

It's entertaining enough and easy to play on the steam deck, but it just makes me appreciate vampire survivors more. Maybe if it gets more updates it will become more polished, but there is an underlying difference that gets me frustrated that I don't think can be easily improved. The game is rng. Many items are way better than others, especially for certain builds. Getting certain weapons or tomes early makes a huge difference. Likewise rolling an early legendary such as dragonfire or getting the turbo skates is a massive boost. What this can mean is you can also just get shafted by item drops, spawn location, or weapon/tome choice.

This makes doing things like the challenges or the quests, more about rng than skill.

Vampire Survivors was more about, if I figure out how to do things and do it well, I can beat this. Meanwhile this feels more like, if I restart enough times I can get an optimal enough run to do it. Beating the stage boss in under x min is way easier when it's right next to your spawn.

This game looks a lot like Vampire Survivors but 3D, but I promise you it's a lot different. To do well in this game you don't just walk vaguely near enemies, level up, walk vaguely near enemies, level up... etc.. Your best bet is to learn to move fast. This game has movement tech that will serve you well when you get the game of it. Go fast, search the map for easy upgrades, scoop up exp gems as you go. Summon the map's boss and lay into it. It makes for a really fun, fast-paced experience that I whole-heartedly recommend. 
The only real hurdle in this game is getting your foot in the door. Learning the movement, which upgrades to prioritize, and how to unlock stuff is your first priority. There are guides available to help you get started.

The game is garbage, there's nothing to scale damage or XP, making you a slave to the damage and XP tomes. That's why all roguelikes have upgrades outside of the levels. The levels are short and there's no time freeze when a boss spawns; enemies simply spawn in front of you and sometimes literally underneath you. When you defeat a boss and go to the next "level," the enemies' HP simply doubles, but the XP gained doesn't scale at all. Overrated game.

It's very fun at first, but suddenly the grind mixed with the insane difficulty spike and forced meta killed it for me. Yes, stans, we see you in every negative review going hard for the dev and this game and if this game is only meant for "badass hardcore gamers", point taken - I'm not the appropriate demographic I guess. I just want to have fun, not be punished by rediculous metrics that scale absurdly.

Fun weapons, fun visual design, fun jokes that don't feel too overbearing or cringey, fun character designs that're fun to play as and feel distinct, fun maps to traverse... I just want more!

Having said that, enemies are fairly easy to work around and minibosses don't feel challenging enough; I want less variations of Stone Golem and more stuff like Scorpionussy. Desert is my favourite map because the enemy variety makes it more fun to play.

The Stage and Final Bosses are also pretty meh. Doesn't bother me too much because the fun for me is in the movement and the builds leading up to the bosses, but I only enjoy fighting Big Bob. The Forest and Desert bosses are too easy and too annoying respectively.

Oh, and the game is pretty limited in builds once you get to the Leaderboard. ...But I never play for a place on the Leaderboard, so that doesn't bother me.
